### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained A41 and A26, and exactly one of four alternative activities appeared between them: A14 in about 21 in 100 traces, A16 in about 26, A17 in about 25, and A18 in about 29 (the shares sum to roughly all traces, and these activities never co-occurred). Whichever of the four occurred was always followed by A26. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL002, REL018, REL025]
- In the later window, none of A14, A16, A17 or A18 was observed (0 of 200 traces), while A15, A23, A24 and A25 — absent earlier — each occurred exactly once in every trace (200 of 200). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- In the later window, A41 precedes each of A15, A23, A24 and A25 in every trace, and each of them precedes A26 in every trace; the four always co-occur but with no fixed pairwise order (for example, A15 comes before A23 in about 53 in 100 traces and after it in about 48 in 100; A24 before A25 in about 45 in 100 and after it in about 55 in 100). [REL013, REL016, REL017, REL036, REL038, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL043, REL044]
- A41's outgoing transitions shifted from A14/A16/A17/A18 (about 21%, 26%, 25% and 29% of its outgoing edges) to A15/A23/A24/A25 (about 28%, 27%, 21% and 24%). Each new activity is followed by any of the other three or by A26 with roughly equal shares (about 20–34% each). [DIR002, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- The distance from A41 to A26 changed from 2 event positions in all traces before to 5 event positions in all traces after; A26's mean relative position moved from about 0.39 to 0.45 of the trace, and A41's from about 0.33 to 0.29. [LAG001, POS009, POS010]
- A26 and A41 themselves remained in every trace in both windows, so their participation did not change. [POS009, POS010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A41 and A26 was restructured: in the earlier window each trace executed exactly one of four alternative activities (A14, A16, A17 or A18) between A41 and A26, whereas in the later window that single step appears replaced by a block in which A15, A23, A24 and A25 each execute once in an order that varies from trace to trace, placing A26 five positions after A41 instead of two. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC006, DIR009, LAG001, REL013, REL016, REL017]

Seventy-two evidence items qualified, many times the roughly 0.62 expected by chance for this screening, so the pattern as a whole cannot be explained by random re-splits; each item's difference is also larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits. The change is shown directly by relational evidence (co-occurrence and precedence), by the A41-to-A26 lag, and by successor and position shifts, and the all-or-nothing participation pattern (0 of 200 versus 200 of 200 traces for eight activities) is far beyond what sampling differences in variant frequencies typically produce. [OCC002, OCC006, DIR002, LAG001, REL016]

Limitations remain: zero participation only means A14, A16, A17 and A18 were not observed in the later window, not that they were removed from the process, although their earlier rates of about 21–29 in 100 traces make their absence in 200 traces unlikely if behaviour were unchanged. The many relation items largely restate one underlying restructuring rather than independent confirmations, and the indicators cannot establish the exact rule governing the order of the new block — the near-even directional shares are consistent with, but do not prove, a random ordering. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR002, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
